title: Variant gate probe: economics-first quality gating notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures the current probe design for attaching lightweight economic gates to low-cost model variants so we can (a) lower token spend without materially degrading UX, and (b) measure the marginal cost-of-quality in a way that feeds back to batch/quantization recommendations. Intention is to iterate quickly with product, SRE, and applied ML.

Executive summary (tl;dr):
- Problem: cheap variants (quantized / smaller arch / batching-aggressive) reduce per-token cost but sometimes produce subtle regressions that only surface on some prompts or metrics.
- Proposal: implement two-tier gating at evaluation + online traffic: an off-line eval gate (cohort-level regression check) and a lightweight runtime gate (signal-based holdback) that prevents ramp to cheap variant when quality delta exceeds calibrated thresholds.
- Measurement goal: produce a marginal cost-of-quality curve (delta-cost / delta-quality) per workload bucket and recommend specific config classes to ship (e.g., q4_0 + batch=16 for chat-lightweight).

Design: two complementary gates
1) Eval gate (pre-rollout):
   - Run candidate cheap config through the existing eval harness for representative prompt-sets (anchor + workload shards).
   - Compute metrics: automated rubric score (0-1), BLEU-ish where applicable, hallucination rate proxy, toxicity safety delta.
   - Accept candidate if: weighted_eval_score_drop <= X (suggested initial X = 0.03 absolute) AND critical-failure-rate increase <= Y (Y = 0.004).
   - Important: thresholds are workload-weighted. For high-precision workloads (search, retrieval-augmented workflows) use X=0.01. For casual chat use X=0.06.

2) Runtime micro-gate (early ramp / production):
   - Lightweight signals: per-route perplexity shift, user-feedback p50-rerate, backend quality monitor spike (synthetic gold prompts injected at 0.5% traffic).
   - Policy: start with 5% traffic to variant; if signal breaches threshold (e.g., synthetic-gold-failures > 0.5% of injections in 2h window or perplexity change > 12%), auto-throttle to 1% and notify. If sustained > 4h reversion, auto-fallback.

Metrics and definitions (how we quantify cost-of-quality):
- Unit cost delta: incremental $/1M tokens for variant vs baseline (from cost model spreadsheet).
- Quality delta: relative change in weighted_eval_score (signed) for the target workload bucket.
- Marginal cost-of-quality (MCQ) = (unit_cost_delta) / max(0.001, -quality_delta) so we avoid divide-by-zero and interpret bigger MCQ as expensive loss per unit quality.
- Keep historical lanes for MCQ per variant x workload. Use deciles for traffic to capture tail sensitivity.

Spreadsheet model overview (current columns in the working sheet):
- variant_id, baseline_model_id, hardware_profile, qprofile, batch_policy, token_cost_baseline, token_cost_variant, delta_cost_per_token, eval_score_baseline, eval_score_variant, delta_score, MCQ, recommended_action
- Quick sanity numbers: q4_0 on A100: delta_cost_per_token = -$0.0000008, delta_score = -0.015 on conversational set -> MCQ ~= 5.3e-05 (units: $ per eval-score-point).
- We are adding columns for: injection-fail-rate (prod synthetic), rerank-delta (for reranking workloads), perceived-latency-delta.

Experiment plan (two waves):
Wave A (controlled eval + small synthetic injection):
- Run candidates for top 6 workload buckets (customer-sentences, internal-bench-chat, summarization, instruction-following, rerank, embeddings-quality-check).
- Duration: 2 weeks of eval runs + 1 week of aggregated analysis.
- Success criteria: fewer than 2 workload buckets show delta_score < -0.03 AND no critical-failure-rate > 0.01.

Wave B (progressive ramp):
- Canary 1: 0.5% of traffic + synthetic injections. Monitor 24/7 for 72h.
- Canary 2: 5% traffic if canary 1 passes. Hold for 7 days.
- Escalation: automatic rollback if synthetic injection failure > 0.5% in any 24h window or customer-complaint spike (internal signal).

Calibration heuristics / thresholds rationale:
- We prefer to calibrate conservatively at first: small absolute eval drops can be amplified downstream. The thresholds above come from historical regressions in H2-2025 where q4_0 + aggressive batching caused a 2% drop on retrieval BLEU that impacted user satisfaction.
- Use banded thresholds: precise workloads (financial/legal) get tight gates; low-risk chat gets wider gates.

Operationalization notes (how this integrates with product and runtime):
- The eval gate is a step in the rollout pipeline (Console rollout UI will show gate pass/fail with breakdown).
- Runtime micro-gate hooks into router policy: we need a small API that accepts metric increments and returns a holdback decision. SRE to scope endpoints.
- Rollouts dashboard should expose MCQ per variant and include a compare view vs baseline.

Risks and open questions:
- Data representativeness: our eval prompt sets might not cover niche enterprise prompts; need to allow customer-specific anchors.
- Gaming: cheap variant may pass synthetic injections but fail on unseen distribution. Consider dynamic injection selection per-customer.
- Metric alignment: which eval score best correlates with user-perceived quality? We need a small labeling study to correlate eval_score delta to NPS/CSAT proxies.
- Quantization interplay: some qprofiles cause occasional determinism shifts that break downstream tools. Detection logic must include structural output checks (e.g., code-tokenization diffs).

Action items / next steps:
- Product: finalize workload buckets and priority ordering (Ravi).
- Applied ML: run Wave A runs for top 6 buckets and dump results to the shared sheet (Lina).
- SRE: spec the runtime gate API and synthetic injection flow (Marco).
- Growth/Support: define customer-facing wording for potential regressions and fallback (Emily).
- Timeline: aim for Wave A runs complete by 2026-02-20, Wave B canaries ready by 2026-03-05.

Appendix: quick checklist for an evaluation run
- [ ] Ensure anchor prompts reflect production traffic percentiles (p10/p50/p90).
- [ ] Run reward-model scoring and calibrate weights for weighted_eval_score.
- [ ] Compute MCQ and tag any variant with MCQ > threshold T (T TBD; starting probe T = $0.0005 per score-point) as "economically inefficient".
- [ ] Upload raw logs + diff artifacts to linked GCS path and reference in the sheet.

Rough notes / brainstorming fragments:
- Could we compute a per-prompt sensitivity vector that identifies which prompts blow up the score for a variant? If we can, those prompts could be used as targeted guardrails rather than full rollback.
- Consider a hybrid policy: allow cheap variant by default but route top-k prompts (by sensitivity) to baseline. This gives most cost savings while protecting critical cases.
- Short-term hack: if we detect structured-output mismatch (JSON schema), always fall back to baseline independent of eval score.

Comments welcome — leave inline notes or ping in #product-optimize.
